transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Ava Morales (Redwood AE), Rafael Chen (Redwood SE), Maya Patel (Redwood CSM), Tom Alvarez (CTO - Steadfast), Priya Singh (Head of ML), Marcus Lee (Infra), Lena Ortiz (Procurement)

Summary (auto): quick sync on renewal and possible expansion; customer wants better latency in EU, asking about dedicated capacity pricing and contract length; Redwood to run targeted benchmarks and return a contract draft.

Transcript:
[00:00] Ava Morales: hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll give like 45 ish minutes, quick agenda, renewal check-in, expansion ask, perf benchmarks, and next steps. can everyone hear ok?
[00:06] Tom Alvarez: yep good here, thanks Ava.
[00:12] Priya Singh: hi, yes, hearing you.
[00:20] Rafael Chen: hey folks, Rafael from Redwood infra, i'll cover the benchmarks and capacity options.
[00:27] Maya Patel: Maya here, i'll help with usage / billing questions.
[00:33] Lena Ortiz: Lena from procurement, i'll be reviewing contract timing.
[00:38] Marcus Lee: Marcus on infra. quick note we had increased error spikes last month but seem mitigated.
[00:45] Ava Morales: thanks. quick context, your current hosted plan renews in late March, right Tom? we wanted to see if you're sticking with hosted or moving to Dedicated/reserved.
[00:55] Tom Alvarez: yeah renewal is end of month. We're evaluating Dedicated because our EU customers are seeing latency issues, and cost is creeping up with higher token volumes. also curious about adding eu-west-1 and ap-southeast-1 regions.
[01:10] Priya Singh: from an ML perspective, our models are larger now and the KV cache usage is up, so cold-starts are worse. we saw 180-220ms p95 in US but EU is hitting 400ms occasionally.
[01:25] Rafael Chen: got it. Dedicated can reduce tail latency via pinned GPU pools and more predictable batching. we can configure autoscaling and burst, but pricing changes. also we have edge routing so requests from eu can be routed to nearest region if you add eu-west-1.
[01:40] Lena Ortiz: what's the price delta for Dedicated vs hosted? ballpark numbers please.
[01:46] Maya Patel: (interject) i'll send the typical tiered pricing but generally dedicated is a monthly commit plus lower per-token run rates.
[01:55] Ava Morales: high-level: for your current QPS, a modest Dedicated pool would be roughly a 30-40% increase in monthly commit but could cut per-token cost by ~25% and reduce latency p95 by 30-50% in-region. i'll document and send exact numbers.
[02:12] Marcus Lee: does Dedicated support our current V P C setup and SAML S S O? we need SSO for infra team.
[02:19] Rafael Chen: yes, Dedicated supports customer V P C peering and SAML; for Private deployments we also offer an on-prem option but that's heavier. Also K M S integration for envelope encryption is supported.
[02:33] Priya Singh: any gotchas with quantization? we're exploring 4-bit to cut costs but worried about quality regressions.
[02:40] Rafael Chen: we do model-specific quant profiles. we can recommend configs based on your evals; some models tolerate 4-bit fine, others need 8-bit. we'll include recommendations in the benchmark report.
[02:51] Tom Alvarez: one big ask — we need EU-hosted data residency for certain clients, so if we add eu-west-1, can logs/audit remain in region?
[02:59] Ava Morales: yes, we can restrict logs and storage to eu-west-1 for that tenancy; we'll include that in the contract SLRs. we'll check data retention policy for EU tenancy.
[03:10] Lena Ortiz: for procurement, if we do a 12-month extension with a 20% committed volume discount, can you include an SLA credit?
[03:18] Ava Morales: typically yes, SLA credits are negotiable for Dedicated; we'll include standard uptime SLAs and propose credits. i'll put a draft in the contract.
[03:27] Priya Singh: what about fallbacks — if the Dedicated pool is saturated can Redwood auto-route to hosted or a cheaper model variant?
[03:34] Rafael Chen: yes, smart routing can fallback to hosted or to a compatible quantized variant. we can set policies per route — latency-first or cost-first.
[03:44] Marcus Lee: that sounds good. on the technical side, can we run a benchmark with our 3-model stack (chat+generation+embedding) at 10k requests/day profile to get p50/p95/p99 and cost per 1k tokens across regions?
[03:56] Rafael Chen: absolutely. we'll run in eu-west-1 and us-west-2 to show delta. do you have a synthetic load script or should we reproduce from logs?
[04:03] Priya Singh: we can share last month's request patterns and a workload replay script.
[04:10] Rafael Chen: perfect. i'll need the logs and an S3 location or a small datasheet. we'll then run on both hosted and a mirror Dedicated pool.
[04:18] Tom Alvarez: timeline? we need results before final sign-off.
[04:21] Ava Morales: we can aim to deliver the report by 2026-03-09 if you can share the data by 2026-03-05.
[04:28] Tom Alvarez: okay we'll try to get it to you by EOD 3/5.
[04:33] Lena Ortiz: procurement question — if we commit to Dedicated, do we still get Redwood Console analytics included? we rely on token-level cost breakdown.
[04:41] Maya Patel: console is included in Dedicated tiers; longer retention is an add-on. happy to map retention to your needs.
[04:47] Priya Singh: also need to confirm SOC 2 and ISO attestation for renewals. can you resend SOC2 and pen-test summary?
[04:54] Ava Morales: yes will send SOC2 Type 2 and recent penetration test summary. Rafael i'll include security docs in the benchmark bundle.
[05:02] Rafael Chen: noted. also for eu expansion we should consider cold-cache warmup; i can include kv prefix caching strategy to lower p95. sometimes caches are mis-configured causing high tail latency.
[05:13] Marcus Lee: good — our infra team will coordinate. we'll also need suggested autoscale policies, e.g., keep spare capacity for peak hours.
[05:20] Rafael Chen: we'll propose a policy and cost impact table.
[05:25] Ava Morales: let's talk term length. Tom, are you inclined to a 12 or 24 month? discounts improve with longer terms.
[05:31] Tom Alvarez: looking at headcount and budget, 12 months is safer; if the benchmarks and SLA look good we might convert to 24 at renewal.
[05:38] Lena Ortiz: 12 months with an option to convert at 9 months would be ideal so procurement has an out clause.
[05:44] Ava Morales: we can draft a 12-month extension with an option to extend to 24 with 60 days notice. i'll include that.
[05:50] Priya Singh: lastly, on model versions — we need pinning so rollouts don't break prod. does Redwood support canary and A/B rollouts?
[05:58] Rafael Chen: yes, Redwood Console supports canary deploys, A/B experiments, and automatic fallback policies — we'll show examples in the report.
[06:07] Tom Alvarez: great. any other questions?
[06:10] Lena Ortiz: just timeline for contract. we'll need the draft by 3/6 to review internally.
[06:15] Ava Morales: will do. recap of next steps: Ava send pricing + contract draft by 3/6; Rafael run benchmarks and share perf/cost spreadsheet by 3/9; Maya share usage dashboard by 3/5; Tom confirm regions by 3/7; Redwood to share SOC2 + pen-test docs.
[06:33] Priya Singh: sounds good. thanks everyone.
[06:36] Ava Morales: thanks all, we'll follow up via email and post the benchmark run in the shared folder. bye.

Notes: transcription contains minor mis-hearings ("V P C" etc). references to Redwood Dedicated, Console, KV cache, K M S, SOC2. Links referenced during call: Redwood pricing spreadsheet (link shared in chat), benchmark template (link), SOC2.pdf (to be shared).

End of transcript.
